extraction.name: CONTEXTUAL
extraction.description: A context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning dataset consisting of 506 challenging instructions for Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) evaluation, covering eight real-world scenarios with text-rich images.
extraction.creator: Rohan Wadhawan, Hritik Bansal, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng
extraction.publisher: Proceedings of the 41stIntemational Conference on Machine Leaming , Vienna, Austria. PMLR 235
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from six different sources including LAION-5B, Rico Dataset, Open WebText Initiative, and existing VQA datasets. Images were filtered manually or heuristically, and then annotated by the authors with human-written instructions and responses.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: LAION-5B, Rico Dataset, Open WebText Initiative, InfographicVQA, STVQA, and ESTVQA datasets.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images underwent manual filtering for suitability or heuristic-based filtering using PaddleOCR to detect text, selecting the top 500 images with the highest number of words.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Authors were divided into two groups to annotate specific categories following guidelines. MTurk workers verified the correctness of each sample. Incorrect samples were filtered out, and each author group reviewed the samples created by the other group.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: MTurk workers verified the correctness of each sample, finding 96% were annotated correctly. Incorrect samples were filtered out, and author groups cross-reviewed samples to ensure adherence to guidelines and filter out low-quality samples.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and code are made available along with a continuously updated leaderboard.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No apparent harmful and privacy sensitive information was observed.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset evaluates models that can power real-world applications such as interpreting text-rich scenes for assisting the visually impaired.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Linguistic diversity and writing style of the human responses may change with different social groups, which could impact the human baseline performance.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Human evaluations are hard to scale and expensive. The annotators were mainly from the US, which may limit the reliability of human evaluation results across diverse regions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning capabilities of large multimodal models.

name.evidence: In this paper, we introduce CONTEXTUAL , a novel dataset featuring human-crafted instructions that require context-sensitive reasoning for text-rich images.

description.evidence: To evaluate multimodal models’ capability of jointly reasoning over embedded text and visual context in text-rich images, we propose CONTEXTUAL , aContext-sensitive Text-rich vis ualreasoning dataset consisting of 506challenging instructions for LMMs evaluation. CONTEXTUAL covers eight real-world scenarios with text-rich images

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The images that are categorized under Time ,Shopping ,Navigation , and Abstract undergo manual filtering to guarantee their suitability for annotation. However, for Application Usage ,Web Usage ,Infographic , and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes , we perform heuristicbased filtering. Specifically, we employ a PaddleOCR (paddlepadle, 2023) to detect the text in the image. Subsequently, we select the top 500 images with the highest number of words

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We divide the authors into two groups, namely Group 1 and Group 2, each responsible for annotating four specific categories. The authors strictly adhered to the provided annotation guidelines throughout the annotation... we asked MTurk workers... to verify the correctness of each sample... we tasked each author group to review the samples created by the other group.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: we asked MTurk workers (mutually exclusive from the ones used for human performance baseline and human evaluation) to verify the correctness of each sample

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: we asked MTurk workers... to verify the correctness of each sample < image, instruction, response > and found that 96% of the samples were annotated correctly. Filtering out the incorrect samples, we tasked each author group to review the samples created by the other group. This ensured adherence to guidelines and filtered out low-quality samples.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: we show each model response, without revealing the model identity, to three human annotators independently.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: In our experiments, we asked human annotators, mainly from the US, to provide responses to establish a human baseline.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: We make the dataset and code available to the LMM community along with a continuously updated leaderboard with recent LMMs.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: we did not observe any apparent harmful and privacy sensitive information in them.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: The ability to reason about the interactions between the text and visual context in the images powers many real-world applications. For example, interpreting text-rich scenes (e.g., navigating maps in public spaces) for assisting the visually impaired

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We are aware that the linguistic diversity and writing style of the human responses would change with different social groups. The extension of our work can focus on understanding the impact of different social groups on the human baseline performance

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Since human evaluations are hard to scale and expensive, we also perform automatic evaluation... To obtain more reliable human evaluation results, future work would involve annotators from more diverse regions.
